newsitem.title: USA: IBM to unveil speech system for radiologists.
newsitem.headline: IBM to unveil speech system for radiologists.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. said it will introduce Thursday a speech recognition system that will let radiologists dictate and edit patient reports directly into their personal computer.

The system, called MedSpeak/Radiology, has a vocabulary of 25,000 words an accuracy rate of over 95 percent. It is the first real-time continuous speech product in IBM's new VoiceType family of speech recognition products.
IBM said by using the system, which is made up of software and a noise cancellation microphone, radiologists can work more efficiently and cut healthcare costs.

Typically, a radiologist, who interprets X-rays, Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) and CAT scans, dictates patient information into a tape recorder that is later transcribed by a typist, and then reviewed again by the radiologist, a process that can take several hours to days. The MedSpeak system reduces the turnaround time and transcription costs and increases patient confidetiality.
IBM researchers developed the MedSpeak/Radiology system by working with radiologists from the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Centre in New York and Massachusetts General in Boston.
The system is made up of software and a special noise cancellation microphone, handheld or headset.

The system requires a personal computer with a PentiumPro microprocessor with a speed of 200 megahertz and runs on Microsoft Corp.'s Windows NT operating system. No special training of the software is required for most native North American English speakers.

The Medpseak/Radiology system with a handheld microphone costs $4,495 and with a headset microphone for $4,395. The systems will be available from IBM or its business partners in the United States and Canada, starting Sept. 17.
